messages.subject: bilat.symmetry vs. procD.lm results?
parts:
I am trying to check my understanding of asymmetry analyses by comparing a Procrustes ANOVA in procD.lm() to the results of using bilat.symmetry(). My intuitive guess was that they should produce very similar ANOVA tables for shape. However, that's not exactly what I got.

Code:

data(mosquito)
Y.gpa <- gpagen(mosquito$wingshape)
gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = Y.gpa$coords,
                           ind = mosquito$ind, #for some reason, "individual" or "critter" didn't work, only "ind" did.
                           side = mosquito$side,
                           replicate = mosquito$rep)
wing.sym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, side=side,data = gdf, #modelling code from examples in manual
                          object.sym = FALSE, RRPP = TRUE, iter = 150)
wing.anova<-procD.lm(shape ~ ind + side + ind/side, data= gdf, iter=150)  #same compared to model in guts of bilat.symmetry() code?


Results:
> wing.sym$shape.anova
                   Df       SS        MS     Rsq      F        Z Pr(>F)  
ind                 9 0.103909 0.0115455 0.45510 2.6871  1.53745  0.062 .
side                1 0.003195 0.0031951 0.01399 0.7436 -0.47277  0.681  
ind:side            9 0.038670 0.0042967 0.16937 1.0410  0.27242  0.389  
ind:side:replicate 20 0.082546 0.0041273 0.36154                        
Total              39 0.228321      

> summary(wing.anova)

Analysis of Variance, using Residual Randomization
Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals
Number of permutations: 151
Estimation method: Ordinary Least Squares
Sums of Squares and Cross-products: Type I
Effect sizes (Z) based on F distributions

          Df       SS        MS     Rsq      F       Z   Pr(>F)  
ind        9 0.104888 0.0116542 0.45533 2.7995  5.0350 0.006623 **
side       1 0.003221 0.0032209 0.01398 0.7737 -0.2641 0.596026  
ind:side   9 0.038990 0.0043323 0.16926 1.0407  0.2068 0.417219  
Residuals 20 0.083259 0.0041629 0.36143                          
Total     39 0.230358  

Most of the values are similar, but not identical (and the SS and MS should be identical, right?). More worryingling, the effect size and p-value for individual variation is very different. My understanding is that result that must mean that the shape of the permutation-derived null distribution must be different between the two models which means that I've misspecified the null model for testing the effect of "individual" in the Procrustes ANOVA. Is this a linear modelling mistake on my part? Am I missing an important part of theory? I apologize if I'm asking about a simple mistake in a GMM forum, but I'm out of ideas for what I could fix to be able to convince myself that the two approaches are essentially the same (which was my understanding of the bilat.asymmetry process).

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] bilat.symmetry vs. procD.lm results?
parts:
Natasha,

 

There were two implementation errors in your example that caused the discrepancies.

 

First, because this is a nested model, one must specify the ‘ind:side’ as the error for the main effects of ‘ind’ and ‘side’ for your procD.lm approach.  This will generate the proper F-values, effect sizes, and p-values 

 

Second, your use of bilat.symmetry was not quite correct. Notice in the help file that if one performs GPA prior to running bilat.symmetry, then one provides bilat.symmetry with the gpagen object, not its components. You provided the components, meaning that another gpagen was performed within bilat.symmetry: resulting in slight rotational differences (and thus the SS differences in the 3rd or 4th digit).

 

Here is your example again, with corrected code. Note now that the methods yield identical results.

data(mosquito)

Y.gpa <- gpagen(mosquito$wingshape)

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = Y.gpa$coords,

                           ind = mosquito$ind, #for some reason, "individual" or "critter" didn't work, only "ind" did.

                           side = mosquito$side,

                           replicate = mosquito$rep)

## NOTE what one puts in 'A'

wing.sym <- bilat.symmetry(A = Y.gpa, ind = ind, side=side,data = gdf,

                           object.sym = FALSE)

wing.anova<-procD.lm(shape ~ ind + side + ind/side, data= gdf)

 

wing.sym$shape.anova

 

## NOTE specification of error terms for main effects

anova(wing.anova, error = c("ind:side", "ind:side","Residuals"))

> wing.sym$shape.anova

                   Df       SS        MS     Rsq      F        Z Pr(>F)

ind                 9 0.104888 0.0116542 0.45533 2.6901  1.53968  0.061 .

side                1 0.003221 0.0032209 0.01398 0.7435 -0.47265  0.681 

ind:side            9 0.038990 0.0043323 0.16926 1.0407  0.27074  0.390 

ind:side:replicate 20 0.083259 0.0041629 0.36143                        

Total              39 0.230358                                          

---

Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

 

> anova(wing.anova, error = c("ind:side", "ind:side","Residuals"))

Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals
Number of permutations: 1000

Estimation method: Ordinary Least Squares

Sums of Squares and Cross-products: Type I
